headline: Issued compliance certificate, two wetlands determinations, and a tree-removal enforcement order
summary: The Commission issued a Certificate of Compliance for 110-228 Common Lane, approved determinations of applicability for 5 Hawk Hill Road and 222 Dodge Street, and continued the 228 Common Lane request to April 28, 2026. It also issued an enforcement order for unpermitted tree removal at 140 Hart Street, approved mileage expenditures, and approved March 18, 2026 minutes as amended.
decisions: Issued a Complete Certificate of Compliance for 110-228 Common Lane, DEP File #5-1405, including perpetual conditions #37-40, 5-0.
Issued a Negative 4 and Negative 6 Determination of Applicability for 5 Hawk Hill Road, 5-0.
Issued a Negative 2 Determination of Applicability for 222 Dodge Street with conditions as discussed, 5-0.
Issued an Enforcement Order for 140 Hart Street requiring a restoration planting plan by April 21, 2026, to be presented at the April 28, 2026 meeting, 5-0.
Continued the Request for Determination of Applicability for 228 Common Lane to April 28, 2026, 5-0.
Approved Conservation Agent March mileage of $21.84 and Conservation Field Inspector March mileage of $8.71, 5-0.
Approved the March 18, 2026 meeting minutes as amended, 4-0-1 with Charles abstaining.

compromised during the last storm, but this work would still require approval. Approximately 97 
ten trees were removed. Some of the trees removed were a few feet from the stream. 98 
 99 
Jeffrey Burbank, owner, explains that there is a road culvert in this area, which is dry most of the 100 
year. They did not know this was a wetland area. He apologizes and states that they would like to 101 
make this right. 102 
 103 
Dennis Silvio, Iron Tree Service, states that the trees were cut from the driveway using a crane. 104 
There was snow on the ground when the trees were cut so it was unclear that a wetland was 105 
nearby. A couple of the trees removed may have been taken down by National Grid last summer. 106

Bertoni states that the flush cutting, though not permitted, does not seem to have damaged the 108 
buffer zone or resource area. The Commission discusses restoration plantings, including six 109
